subject: anatomy
title: Vertebral column
summary: The flexible column of vertebrae that supports the head and trunk and surrounds the spinal cord.

subject: anatomy
title: Spinal cord
summary: The part of the central nervous system inside the vertebral column, linking the brain with the spinal nerves.

subject: chemistry
title: Atoms, elements, molecules and compounds
summary: The four words chemistry uses to describe what things are made of.

subject: chemistry
title: Reading a chemical formula
summary: What the letters, the small numbers and the big numbers in a formula mean.

subject: chemistry
title: Covalent and ionic bonds
summary: The two main ways atoms hold together: sharing electrons, or attraction between charged ions.

subject: chemistry
title: What is a mole?
summary: The chemist’s counting unit: one mole is 6.022 × 10²³ particles.

subject: chemistry
title: Molar mass
summary: The mass of one mole of a substance, in grams per mole; it converts grams to moles.

subject: chemistry
title: Balancing a chemical equation
summary: Choosing coefficients so every element has the same number of atoms on both sides.
terms: how do I balance an equation

subject: chemistry
title: Using a mole ratio
summary: Turning moles of one substance into moles of another with a balanced equation.

subject: chemistry
title: Molarity
summary: Concentration as moles of solute per litre of solution (mol/L, written M).

subject: chemistry
title: Dilution
summary: Adding solvent lowers the concentration; the moles of solute stay the same, so C₁V₁ = C₂V₂.
terms: how do I calculate a dilution

subject: chemistry
title: Water
summary: H₂O: a bent molecule whose polarity explains much of its behaviour as a liquid and a solvent.

subject: chemistry
title: Electron-pair geometry and molecular structure (VSEPR)
summary: Electron pairs around a central atom spread as far apart as possible; the shape named after the atoms alone is the molecular structure.

subject: chemistry
title: Reading a molecule model
summary: What the spheres, sticks and colours in the 3D molecule viewer mean, and what they leave out.

subject: chemistry
title: Acids and bases
summary: An acid gives away a hydrogen ion (H⁺); a base accepts one.

subject: chemistry
title: pH
summary: A number describing how acidic a solution is: pH = −log[H₃O⁺].

subject: chemistry
title: Neutralisation
summary: An acid and a base react to form a salt and water.

subject: chemistry
title: Ideal gas law
summary: PV = nRT links a gas’s pressure, volume, amount and temperature.

subject: chemistry
title: Exothermic and endothermic changes
summary: Some changes release heat to their surroundings; others take heat in.

subject: physics
title: Position in free fall
summary: The height of an object moving only under gravity, as a function of time, when up is taken as positive.

subject: mathematics
title: Power rule for derivatives
summary: The derivative of xⁿ is n·xⁿ⁻¹.

subject: biology
title: Enzyme catalytic cycle
summary: An enzyme binds its substrate at the active site, lowers the activation energy of the reaction, releases the products and is ready to act again.

subject: biology
title: Michaelis–Menten equation
summary: The initial rate of an enzyme-catalysed reaction as a function of substrate concentration.

subject: biology
title: Substrate needed for 90% of Vmax
summary: Rearranging the Michaelis–Menten equation to find the [S] that gives a chosen fraction of the maximum rate.
